O laço mais rápido: cada motor segue o â: The fastest loop: each motor follows the requested angle with a PD controller. On the robot it runs in the manufacturer's SDK; in MuJoCo, it is the G1's position actuator (kp=500) at every 2 ms step. In Figure's Helix 02, S0 became a learned controller running at 1 kHz.
O resultado: juntas, IMU e contato dos p: The result: joints, IMU and foot contact go back to the upper layers every cycle. If S1 gets the balance wrong, no fast S0 can save the robot (lesson 4 shows this).

Controle de humanoide era montado em blo: Humanoid control was built from hand-written blocks: a step planner, the foot's trajectory in the air, the support leg, and balance via ZMP or MPC (model predictive control).
Funciona e é interpretável, mas cada hab: It works and it is interpretable, but every new skill needs new engineering. Lesson 6 of FTH course 0 showed the center of mass and the support polygon behind it.
O caminho aberto virou: captura ou vídeo: The open path became: human motion capture or video → retargeting (GMR) → a motion tracking policy trained with PPO across thousands of simulations (BeyondMimic, GMT, SONIC) → sim2sim → robot.
Uma política só imita qualquer movimento: One policy imitates any reference motion and serves as the base for teleoperation and for the VLA. Figure described the same thing in Helix 02: a 10M-parameter controller at 1 kHz, trained on more than 1.000 h of human motion, which replaced 109.504 lines of C++.

O controle de corpo inteiro: transforma: Whole-body control: it turns the "what" into angles for all the joints at once, while keeping balance. This is the subject of this course.
